# acp

Agent Client Protocol: local and TCP transports, server and client.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-acp.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-acp.el)
- **Loaded:** by default
- **Requires:** nothing
- **Required by:** [acp-remote](acp-remote.md), [ui](ui.md)

## About

The only way a UI talks to the harness.  This file is both halves of
the Agent Client Protocol (ACP, JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line):

- The server side turns bus methods into ACP methods and bus events
  into `session/update` notifications.  Standard ACP methods
  (`initialize`, `session/new`, `session/prompt`, ...) are mapped by
  hand; every other bus method under an allowed prefix is callable
  as `_harness/NAME` with its arguments passed by name.

- The client side (`harness-acp-connect`, `harness-acp-request`,
  `harness-acp-notify`, `harness-acp-set-handler`) is what every UI
  module codes against.  A local connection dispatches Lisp objects
  straight into the server without JSON; a TCP connection speaks the
  wire protocol to a harness running elsewhere.  Both deliver the
  same shapes: everything a client receives is wire-normalised
  (symbols become strings), so a UI is written once.

Nothing here blocks: transports use process filters, results are
promises, and every callback into a client runs from the command
loop, never inside the caller's frame: what a client receives is
queued and handled from a timer, a slice at a time, so that a burst
of messages leaves Emacs time to redisplay and read input between
slices (see "Client: receiving").  Where Emacs's event loop may leave
a socket unread until the next input event, as GUI Emacs on macOS
can, a timer reads the client's sockets as well (see "Client:
polling the sockets").

The module has no requirements.  The server dispatches to whatever
bus methods exist, so it loads and the client API works even when
the session or agent modules are absent.

## Provides

### Methods

- `acp/start` (&rest opts) — Start the ACP TCP server; OPTS `:host` and `:port` override the defaults.
- `acp/status` — Return (:running BOOL :host :port :clients N) for the TCP server.
- `acp/stop` — Stop the ACP TCP server and disconnect its TCP clients.
- `client/request` (method params) — Send request METHOD with PARAMS to the connected clients (the UI).
- `emacs/attached` — Return the Emacsen lent to the harness, the one `emacs/request` asks first.
- `emacs/request` (method params) — Send `_harness/emacs/METHOD` with PARAMS to the Emacs lent to the harness.
- `harness/api` — Describe the bus (methods, events, filters, modules) in wire shape.
- `harness/call` (method args) — Call bus METHOD with the arguments printed in ARGS; return (:value PRINTED).
- `harness/modules` — Describe every module of the harness, as `harness-module-descriptions` does.
- `harness/version` — Return the harness and Emacs versions.

### Hooks

- `harness-acp-agent-capabilities-functions` — Functions adding to the `agentCapabilities` `initialize` answers a client.
- `harness-acp-auth-methods-functions` — Functions returning extra auth methods `initialize` advertises to a client.
- `harness-acp-authenticate-functions` — Functions answering `authenticate` for the auth methods they advertise.
- `harness-acp-authorize-functions` — Functions deciding that a client may call methods without authenticating.
- `harness-acp-initialize-extras-functions` — Functions adding to the `_harness` object `initialize` answers a client.
- `harness-acp-received-hook` — Hook run after each slice of received messages, before Emacs redisplays.

### Options

- `harness-acp-allow-remote` — When non-nil the ACP server may bind a non-loopback address.
- `harness-acp-client-poll-interval` — Seconds between polls of the open TCP client connections, or nil for none.
- `harness-acp-host` — Address the ACP server binds by default.
- `harness-acp-port` — TCP port of the ACP server.  0 picks an ephemeral port.
- `harness-acp-receive-slice` — Longest time, in seconds, a client spends on received messages in one go.
- `harness-acp-token` — Shared secret for TCP clients, or nil for no authentication.
